strength: Known nine creatures in an unknown order with Lighting-driven reveals gives deduction and push-your-luck in nine cards; huge skill expression (random 0%, greedy 5%, lookahead 81%).
weakness: The nine-lives persistence layer is uneven: Ghost lift ranges from +0 (Moth, Mouse, Spider) to +44 (Owl, Fox, Crow), and Glow, Silk and Carry are near-dead, so not every card matters.

closest_existing_game.name: 9-Bit Dungeon (format); Nine Lives: Rogue-and-Write (theme and title)

required_changes: Rework Ghosts so each gives roughly +5 to +25 points: real effect for Moth, Mouse, Spider; Ghost Danger 2 for Owl, Fox, Crow (KPI: single-Ghost lift in range)
Revive Glow, Silk and Carry and test Carry with a bot that models it (KPI: each trick used in at least 15% of runs where Ready; zero dead cards)
Close the five rule ambiguities, incl. Hound-known wording and Ghost free-trophy wording (KPI: zero ambiguities; clarity)
Cut at least one rule or state, for example the Crow's Thief (KPI: clarity, casual rules_simplicity)
Rename the game to avoid Nine Lives: Rogue-and-Write (originality, market fit)
Fix the reference bot's shove loop and unclear steps and re-measure exhaustively; keep Claws 2 (KPI: reference bot 25-60%, median length at least 7)
Only if human sessions show a grindy opening: free Peek or one starting trophy
revision_reason: Yes: Ghost, trick and ambiguity problems have clear diagnoses and cheap tests, and one pass should lift the average from 3.33 past 3.5; do not tune Claws or chase the 40-60% band with bots, and get human solo sessions after.
